requirements.text: nested replies within documented storage/depth limits; sort by best, top, new; vote up / down / clear; live score and rank changes for open threads
thread read p99 < 150 ms; no lost or double-counted votes; hot posts take thousands of votes per second; scores may lag a few seconds
How will you model and query deeply nested comment trees with high read throughput?
How will you handle hot-post vote storms without overwhelming the database with write locks?
How will you compute top and best comment rankings and stream updates to connected clients?

problem.scope: Design a discussion platform supporting deeply nested comment trees and live upvote/downvote tallies. Out of scope: moderation and spam; notifications; search. Performance numbers are study targets, not measurements.

assumptions: Shown depth is capped (e.g. 5) with "continue this thread" links
A user’s own votes are fetched per user and merged on the client, never stored in shared caches
Materialized path segments are unambiguous and allocated transactionally; maximum stored depth and sibling counts are explicit. Rendering depth is independently bounded.
Vote operation receipts and expected vote versions prevent delayed retries from undoing newer intent. Counter deduplication/checkpoints are durable and atomic with count changes.
Reference tests model bounded mechanisms; they do not qualify production concurrency, failure recovery or latency.
solutions.chooseWhen: Counts are maintained as votes arrive, so reads never sum votes; a keyed pipeline turns vote storms into batched writes and pushes rank changes.
